question: In all of the following enzyme deficiencies, hyperammonemia is a common feature, EXCEPT:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Argininosuccinate synthetase deficiency" -> "urea cycle disorder" -> "inability to convert citrulline to argininosuccinate" -> "accumulation of ammonia" -> "hyperammonemia" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase (CPS-I) deficiency" -> "urea cycle disorder" -> "inability to synthesize carbamoyl phosphate from ammonia" -> "accumulation of ammonia" -> "hyperammonemia" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Ornithine Transcarbamoylase (OTC) deficiency" -> "urea cycle disorder" -> "inability to convert ornithine and carbamoyl phosphate to citrulline" -> "accumulation of ammonia" -> "hyperammonemia" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Ornithine Amino Transferase deficiency" -> "gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina" -> "does not involve urea cycle directly" -> "no direct accumulation of ammonia" -> "no hyperammonemia" -> 90%
analysis: The question focuses on identifying which enzyme deficiency does not commonly result in hyperammonemia. Hyperammonemia is a condition characterized by elevated levels of ammonia in the blood, typically associated with defects in the urea cycle. The urea cycle is a critical pathway in the liver for converting ammonia to urea, which is then excreted in the urine. Argininosuccinate synthetase, Carbamoyl Phosphate Synthetase (CPS-I), and Ornithine Transcarbamoylase (OTC) are all enzymes involved in the urea cycle. Deficiencies in any of these enzymes can disrupt the cycle, leading to the accumulation of ammonia and subsequent hyperammonemia. In contrast, Ornithine Amino Transferase (OAT) deficiency affects a different metabolic pathway primarily involved in the synthesis of proline from ornithine in the retina. This condition, known as gyrate atrophy of the choroid and retina, does not typically involve the urea cycle or lead to hyperammonemia. Therefore, based on the standard medical knowledge and the consensus on metabolic pathways involved, Ornithine Amino Transferase deficiency is the correct answer as it does not commonly feature hyperammonemia.
